A promo game concept for DryAire Rentals

The Pitch

A branded game your customers actually finish — and remember — built on a runner format that has already proven itself in play.

01The problem it solves

In a refinery turnaround, wet instrument air is downtime — and downtime is the most expensive line item on the job. DryAire's whole business is keeping that air clean and dry, around the clock, with 75+ years of experience behind it. But a rental dryer is a hard thing to make memorable at a trade show, in an inbox, or on a customer's phone.

Texas Oil Runner puts DryAire in the customer's pocket — a rich, golden-hour Texas game where dry air is literally what keeps the run alive.

02The game

A three-lane runner down a Texas refinery road, rebuilt with richly painted AAA endless-runner art — detailed shading, drifting dust, soft shadows and a refinery glowing in the sunset. The player is a DryAire hand — yellow hard hat, orange vest, work gloves and boots — sprinting toward the refinery skyline past pumpjacks, tank farms and longhorn country.

  • Collect: golden oil drops, plus rare glowing Texas stars worth bonus points
  • Dodge: oil barrels and piles of coiled hoses to jump, pipe racks to slide under, pumpjack arms, the twin-tank DryAire dryer skid and a tall wooden oil derrick to swerve around
  • DryAire Dryer perk: a rental dryer unit rolls in as a shield that eats one crash
  • Golden Wrench perk: pulls nearby drops straight to the runner
  • Hard Hat perk: a speed burst for big distance
  • On the road: DryAire signs read DRYAIRE · BEAUMONT TX · 24/7 · CLEAN DRY AIR the whole run
  • Contact, always one tap away: 1-855-4-DRYAIR sits on the title and end screens
  • Plays anywhere: phone, tablet or desktop — keyboard, swipe or tap controls

04How it goes out

The game ships as a single link or a single file — the same delivery already proven with earlier games in this series. Email it, text it, print the link on a real business card or a trade-show banner with a QR code. No app store, no install, no login. It opens and plays on the phone already in the customer's hand.
